title: Unramified schemes over a field are disjoint unions of finite separable spectra
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] if and only if $X$ is a disjoint union (possibly empty and with an arbitrary index set) of spectra $\operatorname{Spec}L_i$, where each $L_i/k$ is a finite separable algebraic field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), parts (1) and proof, lines 7790-7821

proof.text: Assume f : X → Spec k is unramified. For each point x choose an affine open immersion a : Spec C → X containing x, using Scheme.exists_Spec_apply_eq. Equip C with the k-algebra structure corresponding under Spec.preimage to a ≫ f. Local finite type and formal unramifiedness restrict along the open immersion by Mathlib locality; the diagonal characterization gives the hypotheses of the affine unramified-algebra decomposition. Obtain a k-algebra equivalence e : C ≃ Π_j L_j, with each L_j finite separable over k.

source.place: Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), proof of (1), affine expansion via Algebra Tag 00UW (lemma-unramified-at-prime), proof, and Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field); restriction Tag 02G6 (lemma-unramified-characterize)

proof.text: The map b = Spec(e) is an isomorphism. Pull a point above x back along b. The finite-product-spectrum theorem identifies its prime ideal with the kernel of exactly one factor projection and places it in the image of the open immersion q : Spec L_j → Spec(Π_j L_j). Thus c = q ≫ b ≫ a is an open immersion with image {x}. It is over k: the algebra-equivalence identity e(algebraMap k C r) = algebraMap k (Π_j L_j) r, evaluated at j, identifies c ≫ f with Spec(algebraMap k L_j) by contravariant functoriality.

source.place: Tags 00ED (lemma-spec-product), 00EC (lemma-idempotent-spec), 00E4 (lemma-standard-open), applied to the affine expansion of Morphisms Tag 02G7(1)

proof.text: Choose these finite separable fields L_x and open immersions c_x for all points x. Their ranges {x} are pairwise disjoint, so Mathlib isOpenImmersion_sigmaDesc makes Sigma.desc c an open immersion. Its range is all of X, since each x lies in the range of c_x; hence it is an isomorphism by isIso_of_isOpenImmersion_of_opensRange_eq_top. The coproduct injection identities and the compatibility of each c_x with the structure morphism prove the required compatibility over k. This construction also applies when X is empty and imposes no finiteness on its point set.

source.place: Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), proof of (1), discrete-space/disjoint-union sentence; sheaf axiom spelled out

proof.text: Conversely, given the coproduct presentation over k, each field extension has an etale algebra structure by Algebra.Etale.of_finite_of_isSeparable. RingHom.etale_algebraMap and HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff show that its structure morphism is etale. The given compatibility over k identifies these with the restrictions of e.hom ≫ f to the coproduct summands.

source.place: Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field), finite separable extension paragraph; Morphisms Tags 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), converse, and 02G6 (lemma-unramified-characterize)

proof.text: Apply Mathlib IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover to sigmaOpenCover to deduce that e.hom ≫ f is etale. Compose with e.inv to obtain that f is etale. The etale instances give local finite type and formal unramifiedness; the diagonal characterization gives an open-immersion diagonal. The cover-local proof also includes an empty coproduct.
